newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees higher olive oil output in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees higher olive oil output in 1996/97.

text.p: Global production of olive oil in the 1996/97 (October/September) season is forecast sharply higher at 2.61 million tonnes, up by one million tonnes from the previous season, the independent Oil World newsletter said on Tuesday.
The total sum applied to both pressed and residue oil.
Citing crop increases in Spain, Turkey and Tunisia, Oil World said the expansion in output would lead to a drastic stocks addition although demand was also rising.
World consumption in 1996/97 was pegged at 2.13 million tonnes versus 1.84 million a year earlier, led by Europe, North Africa, Turkey, Syria and others.
End-season stocks were put at 780,000 tonnes at the end of September 1997 after 304,000 tonnes a year earlier.
Spain would more than treble its output to 970,000 tonnes (320,000 in 1995/96), while Italy and Greece were expecting to produce less than last season, Oil World said.
Spanish domestic prices had fallen to 370-390 pesetas per kg in early May from just under 600 pesetas last November, Oil World noted.
Olive oil prices, while well above other vegetable oils, were still attractive to consumers in Spain and other Mediterranean countries, who balked at high sun oil prices.
